description:
We are a team of Code Champs passionate about technology, space exploration, and problem-solving. As beginners in hackathons, we are excited to learn, collaborate, and turn creative ideas into practical solutions using technology. Our interests include programming, web development,space science.
We welcome motivated team members with skills in Java, Python, web development, UI/UX design, research, data analysis, and creative problem-solving.
summary:
What did we develop?
AstroBase – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, cartoon-style web app for children aged 8 to 14. It combines a Space Learning Zone (planets, stars, rockets, astronauts), astronaut mission simulations, quizzes with instant feedback, and rewards such as points, stars and badges. It is built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and LocalStorage saves each learner’s progress.

How does it address the challenge?
Space science can feel distant and hard to picture in traditional lessons. AstroBase turns it into hands-on, game-based learning. Children explore, complete missions and test themselves at their own pace. NASA data such as APOD, the Image and Video Library and Mars Rover photos supports authentic content.

Why is it important?
It builds curiosity about space and science in young learners and makes learning enjoyable instead of passive. It also gives children an age-appropriate digital option that can grow with more missions, AI help and more NASA integrations.
details:
What does your project do, and how does it work?
AstroBase is a web app where children aged 8 to 14 learn about space through play. A child opens the site, explores the Space Learning Zone (planets, solar system, stars, galaxies, astronauts, rockets), starts a mission (Moon Explorer, Mars Exploration, Solar System Explorer, Rocket Launch, Space Station), then takes a quiz with difficulty levels and instant feedback. Points, stars and badges are saved in the browser and shown on an Astronaut Profile. JavaScript handles the missions, quizzes and scoring, and Local Storage keeps progress between visits.

What benefits does it have?

  • Turns a hard subject into a fun, visual experience
  • Children can learn at their own pace
  • Free to open in any browser, with no login or backend needed
  • Quizzes and rewards give instant feedback and motivation

What is the intended impact?
To spark curiosity about space and science in young learners, help them remember what they learn through missions and quizzes, and encourage self-paced digital learning.

What tools did you use?
HTML5 (structure), CSS3 (styling, animations, responsive design), JavaScript (interactivity, quizzes, mission logic), Local Storage (saving progress), and NASA APIs (APOD, NASA Image and Video Library, Mars Rover Photos) for authentic space content.

How is your project creative?
Instead of a plain fact website, AstroBase makes the child an astronaut in training. Learning, missions, quizzes and rewards form one story, and the cartoon style keeps it friendly for kids.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Age-appropriateness: simple language, bright visuals and easy navigation for ages 8–14
  • Accuracy: using authentic NASA content
  • Simplicity: a beginner-friendly stack that a team of four could build and test together
  • Scalability: a modular design, so a backend, more missions and AI help can be added later
  • Engagement: game elements such as points and badges to keep children motivated
